channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Climate Initiatives Highlighted by International Media at COP31
item.description: Foreign media outlets are covering Uzbekistan's climate initiatives presented at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. International agencies focused on the proposals for regional cooperation, combating climate change impacts, and advancing Central Asia's environmental agenda, including a regional climate integration model.

item.title: Uzbekistan Highlights Priorities in Global Climate Policy at COP31
item.description: Uzbekistan is using COP31 in Antalya to advance its sustainable development interests, attract international finance, and forge new technological partnerships. Climate change is a critical issue for Central Asia, impacting water and economic security, agriculture, and energy. For Uzbekistan, efficient water resource management is vital for economic growth due to its reliance on irrigated agriculture.

item.title: Second Belarusian-Uzbek Tourism Forum to be Held in Tashkent
item.description: The second Belarusian-Uzbek tourism forum is scheduled for November 26 in Tashkent. Discussions on preparation involved Belarus's National Tourism Agency director and Uzbekistan's ambassador to Belarus. The Belarusian delegation will also attend the "Silk Road Tourism" international fair.

item.title: Kabul-Nangarhar Highway Closed Due to Heavy Rainfall and Landslides
item.description: The Kabul-Nangarhar highway has been closed to traffic due to heavy rainfall and subsequent landslides and falling rocks. Dozens of vehicles are stranded. The Taliban have reportedly set up a checkpoint in the Darunta area, blocking passage. This follows a weather warning for potential flooding.

item.title: Sewage Spills into Caspian Sea in Mangystau Region Due to Pipe Damage
item.description: Sewage has spilled into the Caspian Sea in the village of Kuryk, Mangystau region, due to damaged pipes, causing an unpleasant odor. Environmentalists confirmed the liquid is sewage and have requested prosecution of the responsible housing and communal services department. The pipe has been repaired.

item.title: Chinese national arrested after stabbing Kazakh workers at gold mine
item.description: A Chinese citizen has been arrested following a conflict with Kazakh workers at a gold mine in the Abai region. One Kazakh worker, aged 27, sustained a knife wound and remains in serious but stable condition in intensive care.

item.title: Astana mayor requests understanding regarding ongoing LRT construction disruptions
item.description: Astana Mayor Zhenis Kassymbek has asked residents for understanding regarding temporary traffic disruptions caused by the second phase of the LRT construction. He stated the project, expected to finish by the end of 2027, will significantly ease traffic congestion.

item.title: Taliban post in Panjshir school set ablaze by 'Green Trend' group
item.description: The 'Green Trend' group, led by Amrullah Saleh, claims to have set fire to a Taliban post located in a school in Panjshir province. Local sources confirmed a fire at the school, damaging several rooms and the roof.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Unified National Test Format to Remain Until 2027, Minister States
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Science and Higher Education, Sayasat Nurbek, confirmed that the Unified National Test (UNT) format will remain unchanged until 2027. A new pilot testing format will be offered as an optional alternative for applicants.

item.title: Turkish and Qatari Companies Win Tender for New Bukhara International Airport
item.description: A consortium of Turkish and Qatari companies, Limak and HBK Contracting, has won the international tender for the New Bukhara International Airport. A 23-year concession agreement is planned with the private partner.

item.title: Astana Drivers Face Another Year of Disruption Due to LRT Construction
item.description: Drivers in Astana will experience traffic disruptions until the end of 2027 due to the ongoing construction of the second phase of the Light Rail Transit (LRT) system. City officials urge understanding, stating the project will significantly ease traffic congestion upon completion.

item.title: Free Cancer Screenings Conducted in Leylek District by National Oncology Center Doctors
item.description: Doctors from the National Oncology and Hematology Center conducted free medical examinations for residents of Leylek district from October 19-23. The initiative, supported by Member of Parliament Ismanali Joroyev, focused on early cancer detection and timely access to medical care. Discussions covered patient conditions and further treatment plans.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Concludes Visit to Turkey for COP31 Summit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev concluded his working visit to Antalya, Turkey, where he attended the opening ceremony of the COP31 Leaders Summit. He delivered a national statement and participated in a high-level event focused on promoting the mountain agenda, glaciers, and cryosphere.

item.title: Construction Start Date for Too-Ashuu – Suyusamyr – Aral Road Announced
item.description: The start date for the construction of the Too-Ashuu – Suyusamyr – Aral road was discussed at an extraordinary meeting of the "Ala-Too" parliamentary group. Preparatory work is complete, and a contract with the contractor is expected by the end of November.

item.title: Bukhara Refinery to Expand Capacity Under $1.8 Billion Project
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand the Bukhara Oil Refinery's capacity as part of a $1.8 billion project. Construction is slated to begin in 2028, with partnerships involving leading technological companies from China, France, the US, and Azerbaijan. The project aims to increase annual output significantly.

item.title: Putin: Foreign Forces in Ukraine Are Unacceptable and Threaten Russia's Security
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that the presence of any foreign forces in Ukraine is unacceptable to Moscow and poses a threat to Russia's national security. He recalled that Russia had consistently opposed this, and that this position was agreed upon in principle during the Istanbul talks.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Unemployment Rate Reached 4.5% in Q3 2026, Youth Unemployment at 2.9%
item.description: In the third quarter of 2026, Kazakhstan's unemployment rate stood at 4.5%, calculated according to the International Labour Organization (ILO) methodology. The unemployment rate among youth aged 15-34 was 2.9%. The total labor force comprised 9.8 million people, with 9.4 million employed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Mandates Banks to Warn Customers About Financial Risks in Credit Advertisements
item.description: Uzbekistan has amended its advertising law, requiring banks to include warnings about potential financial risks in their credit and microloan advertisements. These warnings must occupy at least 10% of the ad space. The law also officially categorizes information on improving financial literacy as social advertising.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Major Expansion of Bukhara Refinery for Over $1.8 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev reviewed plans to expand the Bukhara Oil Refinery, aiming to more than double its processing capacity. The project, costing $1.8 billion, includes modernization for Euro-5 standard fuels and is slated for completion in Q2 2029.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Discusses Afghanistan's Freedom of Expression and Women's Rights in Canada
item.description: UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett met with Canadian journalists to discuss restrictions on freedom of expression, women's rights, and the plight of Afghan journalists. Concerns were raised about girls' exclusion from education and practical measures to hold the Taliban accountable.

item.title: Tashkent Police Foil Robbery Plot at Educational Center
item.description: Tashkent police and the State Security Service have prevented a planned robbery at an educational center. The plot, conceived by a former security guard, involved recruiting acquaintances to steal a large sum of money. Suspects were apprehended before they could execute the plan and flee to a neighboring country.

item.title: Bukhara Refinery to Produce Euro-5 Gasoline from 2029
item.description: The Bukhara Oil Refinery will begin producing Euro-5 standard gasoline in 2029. A project worth $328 million will establish the capacity to produce 1.1 million tons of AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline annually. An additional project, estimated at $1.8 billion, for expanding the plant's capacity was also considered.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Ukraine Foreign Ministers Discuss Trade and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha in Antalya. They discussed bilateral relations, expanding trade and economic cooperation, and regional and international issues. Sybiha informed Saidov about the peace process and the situation in the Black Sea.

item.title: Central Asia's Energy Transition: A Challenge to Move Away from Hydrocarbon Dependence
item.description: Despite significant natural resources, Central Asian countries remain heavily dependent on fossil fuels and imports, particularly from Russia. Facing economic, health, and geopolitical challenges, the five republics are seeking to diversify supplies and accelerate their energy transition for greater independence.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Build Over 2,000 Kilometers of Roads Annually from 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct over 2,000 kilometers of roads each year starting in 2027, according to the deputy minister of transport and communications. In 2026, 1,903 kilometers of roads were asphalted nationwide, a significant increase compared to the previous year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Presidential Election: Digital Signatures and Primaries
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential election process is underway, with 11 candidates, including incumbent Sadyr Japarov. A notable feature is the use of digital technology, specifically the "Tunduk" app, for collecting required signatures. This digital approach presents both opportunities and challenges for candidates and voters.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Achieves Significant Road Construction Milestones in 2026
item.description: A session of the "Ala-Toо" parliamentary group discussed the progress of road construction, irrigation systems, and water supply in Kyrgyzstan. The Deputy Minister of Transport and Communications reported that 1903 kilometers of roads have been asphalted nationwide by 2026, an increase of 735 kilometers compared to the previous year. Future plans aim to construct over 2000 kilometers of roads annually starting from 2027.

item.title: Turkish-Qatari Consortium to Build New Bukhara International Airport
item.description: Uzbekistan Airports announced the completion of a tender for the construction and management of the New Bukhara International Airport. A consortium of Turkey's Limak İnşaat and Qatar's Hamad Bin Khalid Contracting Company won the bid. They will undertake a joint project to build and manage the airport, with a public-private partnership agreement expected soon for 23 years.

item.title: Taliban Prime Minister Meets Russian Deputy Prime Minister to Boost Ties
item.description: Taliban Prime Minister Mullah Mohammad Hassan Akhund held talks with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk to strengthen bilateral relations and expand economic cooperation. The meeting, also attended by foreign ministers, was described as a significant step. Akhund welcomed Russia's recognition of the Taliban, citing improved security for investment.

item.title: Sewage Water Flows into Caspian Sea Near Kuryk Village, Authorities Confirm
item.description: Environmental authorities in the Mangystau region have confirmed that sewage water was flowing into the Caspian Sea near the village of Kuryk. Residents reported a strong odor and suspicious discharges. An inspection revealed a damaged pipeline, and water samples confirmed the contamination. The pipeline owner has been identified.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Fair Alimony System, Strengthen Child Rights Protections
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a fair system for determining alimony amounts based on living costs. The country will also strengthen efforts to combat discrimination against women and children's rights. A system will be created to ensure quality education and talent development for children of citizens working abroad in labor migration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Calls for Strengthening UN Water Architecture at COP31
item.description: Kazakhstan urged strengthening the UN's water architecture during a special event at COP31 in Antalya. The delegation presented the country's achievements in water resource management and its regional priorities. Kazakhstan proposed creating an International Water Organization to enhance UN coordination and effectiveness, a proposal supported by international organizations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Holds Meeting on Preventing Domestic Violence and Supporting Victims
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Ulan Mamatkanov, chaired a meeting on preventing domestic violence, protecting victims, and providing timely support. Discussions focused on interagency cooperation and the effectiveness of current measures. Directives were issued to strengthen prevention efforts and develop a plan for 2027.

item.title: Kazakh Political Analysts Note Increased Anti-Corruption Investigations Against Top Executives
item.description: Political analysts in Kazakhstan conclude that even top managers of major companies are not immune to investigations, indicating a tough stance against corruption. This reflects the state's commitment to the principle of "Law and Order," a cornerstone of the new constitution, ensuring punishment regardless of position or influence, as stated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

item.title: Turkish-Qatari consortium wins tender to build and operate new airport in Bukhara
item.description: A consortium of Turkey's Limak İnşaat and Qatar's HBK Contracting has won the international tender to build and operate a new international airport in Bukhara under a public-private partnership. The project will be implemented on a Build-Transfer-Operate model. The private partner will construct and manage the passenger terminal and related infrastructure, while the state partner will handle the runway and apron.

item.title: Projects to expand Bukhara refinery production capacity presented to president
item.description: Projects aimed at expanding the production capacity of the Bukhara oil refinery were presented to the president. One project, costing $328 million, will enable the production of Euro-5 compliant AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline, with an expected annual output of 1.1 million tons. This initiative is projected to save up to $150 million annually by reducing imported fuel additives.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Anti-Cancer Drug DVC Faces Market Entry Delay Until Mid-2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's anti-cancer drug DVC is now projected to launch in mid-2027, a delay attributed to stringent clinical trial requirements. The Ministry of Science and Higher Education confirmed the first phase's completion and progression to the second. Development is ongoing, with finalization expected by mid-next year before market release.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Fines for Delayed Housing Handover and 10-Year Guarantees
item.description: A new draft law in Uzbekistan may require developers to pay a 0.01% daily fine for delayed housing handover. The legislation also proposes a minimum 10-year warranty for new homes and mandates that at least 70% of construction be financed through banks, strengthening developer accountability.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Bukhara Refinery to Invest $328 Million in Euro-5 Gasoline Production by 2029
item.description: Uzbekistan's Bukhara Refinery will invest $328 million to launch Euro-5 standard gasoline production by the second quarter of 2029. The upgrade aims to produce 1.1 million tons of Euro-5 fuel annually, create 200 jobs, and save up to $150 million yearly by reducing imported fuel additive purchases.

item.title: Astana and Bishkek Suppress Analysts, Losing Touch with Reality
item.description: Authorities in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are increasingly suppressing independent analysts, mirroring tactics used against independent media. This includes digital censorship, criminal cases, and personal blackmail. This crackdown, particularly evident in the post-Kantar period in Kazakhstan, risks alienating experts and leading to social unrest.
